The establishment of the civil service

The most lasting and significant change of the fourth century was the creation of the first permanent civil service in 354. The system was modelled on those in use in the West, notably in the West Frankish Kingdom, but it was modified to include elements appropriate to the Roman world and the needs of the state. The most significant change was that the civil service came to include a system of recruitment to grade, rather than a system of appointment from the local aristocracy. The system was introduced through public examination.
